There's great canvas software besides just Photoshop. I personally want to try playing with https://krita.org/en/, after I'm done with InkScape. Get a good pen tablet; it really helps, as well. The rest, you kinda just get used to it as you go along. It feels weird for a while, and then one day: it doesn't.

I use Procreate on an iPad Pro and an Apple pen. I despise Apple but I've been unhappy with with previous tablets and thought it just wasn't for me. The selling point on this one was the simplicity of the program and the cohesiveness of the hardware makes the experience so smooth and as close to pencil and paper as I've ever experienced. Tried one out in Best Buy. It surprised me.

Eh, I personally have a Bamboo tablet, and it's (to this day) the best one I've ever used. Pressure sensitive, buttons for context menus and right-clicking, erasing, etc. I tape a piece of paper on to it, and it feels 100% indistinguishable from drawing in a notebook with a sharpie.

That alone makes the program I use more-or-less inconsequential, since it's the same feel that I grew up learning to draw with. I don't like being tied down to any one particular piece of software; but that's just me.

I'm with you MrPim. Digital painting is bizarre. I like that you can hit Control Z and delete brushstrokes, but it's like painting in a dream while you're asleep and no matter how hard you try you can't wake up. I'll take regular painting on a canvas in analog any day.
